SPECIFICATION FOR 

COUNTERSINKS 90^ WITH PARALLEL SHANKS 
AND SOLID PILOTS 

(First Revision) _ 


1. Scope — Covers the dimensions and other requirements of countersinks 90° with parallel shanks 
and solid pilots suitable for countersinks according to IS . 3406 (Part 1 )-1986 'Dimensions for 
countersinks and counterbores: Part 1 Countersinks (second revision)'.

3. Tolerances— Tolerances on cutting length (/i) and overall length (/) shall be as given below

4. Material — Shall be as given in IS . 5099-1 983 'Technical supply conditions for twist drills (_/?r5/ 
revision )'. 

5. Hardness — Shall be as given in IS 5099-1983. 

6. Designation — A countersink having Type A, fine series (f) diameter = 80 mm and 
pilot diameter = 4 3 mm, conforming to this standard, and made of high speed steel shall be 
designated as 


Countersink Af 8 x 4.3 IS 5693 


7. General Requirements 

7.1 The countersink shall be right hand cutting, unless otherwise specified 

7.2 The countersinks with diameter r/ up to 5 mm shall have external centres according to IS 2473- 
1975 'Dimensions for centre holes, and shall also have straight flutes 

7.3 The countersinks with diameter d above 5 mm shall have centre holes according to IS 2473- 
1975 and right hand helical flutes, unless otherwise specified 

7.4 Number of flutes shall be two or three at the discretion of the manufacturer 

7.5 When the flutes of countersinks run into the pilot, their edges shall not be removed within the 

length of the pilot 

7.6 Countersinks may be provided with driving tenons according to IS 5360-1969 'Dimensions for 
driving tenons'. 

7.7 Tool Type N shall be supplied according to IS 5099-1 983, unless otherwise specified 

8. Marking — Countersinks shall be marked with designation, -manufacturer's name or trade mark, 

and month and year of manufacture 

8.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards 

9. Protective Coating and Packing 

9.1 Each countersink shall be covered with a suitable rust proofing material and then wrapped in 
non absorbent paper 

9.2 Each countrersink shall be protected by a cover bearing the countersink diameters and 
manufacturer's name or trademark 

10. Sampling — The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall be in accordance with IS 7778 1975 
Methods for sampling small tools' 

11. Selection — Selection of countersinks for countersunk Types A and B are given in Table 1

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1970. In this revision: 

a) Types A and B countersinks have been given in table aligning various dimensions with 
IS . 3406 (Part 1)-1986, 

b) reference to IS : 5099-1983 has been included for material and hardness requirements, 

c) designation clause has been modified incorporating the type of countersink and the thread 
pitch series, 

d) sampling clause has been included, and 

e) surface Finish has been included. 

In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from 

a) ISO 4205-1977 'Countersinks 90° with parallel shank and solid pilots', issued by the 
International organization for Standardization (ISO ), and 

b) DIN 1866-1975 'Parallel shank countersinks 90° with solid pilot’ , issued by the 
Deutsches Institute fiir Normung ( DIN ).
